MUTATIONS: a transport that does not implement push_photo answers Unsupported by default, so no photo is silently sent or reported failed (SPEC-132)
a transport that does not implement prepare_share answers Unsupported by default (SPEC-132)
an unsupported photo is recorded withheld under its own reason, photo_unsupported (SPEC-132)
a photo deferred by quiet hours or a breaker rolls its claim back, so nothing is held or recorded and the caller's retry sends (SPEC-132)
a failed push releases its claim and records nothing, so a later raise is not already_recorded (SPEC-132)
a delivered photo is recorded as one send in the decision ledger under its key (SPEC-132)
a photo asks the ladder's T2, the tier that spends no celebration budget (SPEC-132)
a photo of exactly the Bot API's byte bound is accepted and one byte over it is refused (SPEC-132)
a prepared share is the transport's own outcome, one call, and records no delivery (SPEC-132)
the file id kept is the largest size Telegram answered, wherever it sits in the list (SPEC-132)
a failed photo opens the outage breaker, so the next photo inside the cooldown is refused before any call (SPEC-132)
a caption is counted in UTF-16 units as Telegram counts it, so 513 characters outside the BMP are refused (SPEC-132)

the prepared share asks the same bound function the photo asks, so a caption over the Bot API's limit is refused before any call (SPEC-132 A17, #430); the mutant asks it of an empty caption, so every over-long caption reaches the transport
an over-long share caption answers `Refused` with the photo's own refusal, not the Bot API's `Failed`, so the caller knows the caption is at fault and nothing was attempted (SPEC-132 A17, #430)

the photo and the share ask one bound function, so what the photo accepts the share accepts, member by member (SPEC-132 A17, #430); the mutant makes the photo take any caption, so the two paths disagree on every over-long one
the limit is inclusive, as the Bot API's 0-1024 is, so a caption of exactly 1,024 UTF-16 units is taken by the photo and the share alike (SPEC-132 A17, #430)
